entries.title: I Kings 9:3
segments:
Hallowed; accepted their consecration of the temple to his service. 
 
All sincere and hearty supplications to God will be accepted, and all offerings presented in love to him receive a gracious reward.

entries.title: I Kings 9:6
segments: Continued obedience to God is needful in order to the continuance of his favors; and if those who have been distinguished by his mercies rebel against him, they will be distinguished in their punishment.

entries.title: I Kings 9:8
segments: Which is high; its height shall only make it a more conspicuous object of reproach.

entries.title: I Kings 9:12
segments: Different men have different tastes, which lead them to follow different occupations and live in different places.  Some are attracted by the noise and bustle of cities, others by the stillness and quiet of the country, and both may be where God calls them, and be mutually serviceable to each other.

entries.title: I Kings 9:13
segments: Cabul; the meaning of this word cannot be certainly determined, but it evidently denotes something displeasing.

entries.title: I Kings 9:15
segments:
. 
 
  Millo; a part of the citidel or fortifications of Jerusalem. 
 
  Hazor; in Naphtali. 
 
  Megiddo; in Issachar. 
 
  Gezer; in Ephraim.

entries.title: I Kings 9:17
segments:
Beth-horon; in the tribe of Benjamin. 
 
  Nether; lower.  There were two places of this name, the upper and the lower, with a steep descent between,

entries.title: I Kings 9:18
segments:
Baalath; in the territory of Dan. 
 
  Tadmor; supposed still to be seen in the desert east of Damascus. 
 
The most opulent cities, and the most splendid human works, are liable to become a heap of ruins.  None should therefore set their hearts on them, but all should secure durable riches and righteousness, treasures in the heavens which will never pass away.

entries.title: I Kings 9:25
segments: All who are distinguished by wealth, power, and influence, should also be distinguished for habitual devotion to God, and regular, conscientious attendance upon his worship.

entries.title: I Kings 9:26
segments:
Ezion-geber; near the north end of the east branch of the Red sea. 
 
As commerce is a source of wealth, and seamen are exposed to numerous privations, hardships, dangers, and vices, those who are benefited by their services should, in addition to giving them suitable compensation and temporal comforts, furnish them with the Bible and other good books, and as far as practicable with all the means of grace.

entries.title: I Kings 9:28
segments: Ophir; supposed to be some place either in Arabia, or on the Indian ocean.
